recipes.name: Cottage pie
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the mince for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour, tomato purée and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer gently for 20 minutes until thick. Season to taste.
Meanwhile peel and chunk the potatoes and boil in salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain, then mash with the butter and milk. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Spoon the mince into a 2-litre ovenproof dish, top with the mash, rough it up with a fork and scatter over the cheese.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Cook the peas and serve alongside.

recipes.name: Sausage and mash with onion gravy

ingredients.note: 40g for the mash, 10g for the gravy

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the sausages on a lightly oiled baking tray and roast for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and cooked through.
For the gravy, melt 10g butter with the oil in a pan and cook the onions over a low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden. Stir in the sugar and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Meanwhile boil the peeled, chunked potatoes in salted water for 15–18 minutes. Drain and mash with the remaining butter and the milk; season.
Cook the peas for 3 minutes. Serve the sausages on the mash with peas and plenty of gravy.

recipes.name: Classic fish pie

ingredients.note: 500ml for the sauce, 50ml for the mash
50g for the sauce, 30g for the mash
zest and a squeeze of juice

steps: Peel and chunk the potatoes and boil in salted water for 15–18 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with 30g butter and 50ml milk.
Meanwhile put the fish in a wide pan with 500ml milk, bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 4 minutes. Lift the fish into a 2-litre baking dish and keep the milk.
Melt 50g butter in a pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm milk and simmer for 2–3 minutes until thick and smooth.
Stir the parsley, lemon zest and a squeeze of juice into the sauce, season, then pour over the fish and scatter over the peas. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Spoon the mash on top, fork the surface and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Toad in the hole

ingredients.note: mixed with a splash of cold water

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to rest while the oven heats.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Put the sausages and 20ml oil in a roasting tin (about 30 x 20cm) and roast for 10 minutes.
Working quickly, pour the batter around the sizzling sausages and return to the oven for 25–30 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Don't open the door for the first 20 minutes.
Meanwhile fry the onions in the remaining oil over a low heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden. Add the stock, bring to the boil and stir in the cornflour mix until thickened.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4–5 minutes. Cut the toad into squares and serve with the gravy and broccoli.

recipes.name: Lemon and thyme chicken traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).

Put the potatoes, onion wedges and garlic cloves in a large roasting tin. Add the chicken, skin side up, toss everything with the oil, thyme, salt and pepper, and squeeze over the lemon, tucking the squeezed halves in too.
Roast for 40 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken skin is crisp.
Scatter the green beans into the tin, toss in the juices and roast for 10 more minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink at the bone (75°C on a thermometer).
Squeeze the soft garlic out of its skins over everything and serve straight from the tin.

recipes.name: Beef and ale stew with mash
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Toss the beef in the flour with a little salt and pepper.
Heat half the oil in a large flameproof casserole and brown the beef in two batches, 4–5 minutes each, then set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, onions, carrots and celery and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Return the beef, pour in the ale and stock, add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, bay and mushrooms, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook in the oven for 2½ hours until the beef is very tender.
About 30 minutes before the end, boil the peeled, chunked potatoes for 15–18 minutes, then drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Remove the bay leaves, check the seasoning and serve the stew over the mash.

recipes.name: Lancashire hotpot

ingredients.note: made up with 500ml boiling water (or lamb stock)

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Brown the lamb in the oil in a large flameproof casserole over a high heat, in batches, for about 5 minutes per batch.
Add the onions and carrots and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour, then the stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme and bay. Season and bring to a simmer.
Arrange the potato slices in overlapping layers on top, brush with the melted butter and season.
Cover with a lid and bake for 1½ hours.
Remove the lid and bake for a further 30–40 minutes until the potatoes are golden and crisp at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Mushroom and leek pot pie

ingredients.note: 100ml for the sauce, the rest to glaze

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the leeks for 5 minutes.
Turn up the heat, add the mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes until golden and any liquid has gone. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the stock and 100ml soya milk. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thick, then stir in the mustard, soy sauce and peas. Season.
Tip the filling into a 1.5-litre pie dish. Unroll the pastry over the top, trim and press the edges onto the dish, cut a small steam hole and brush with the rest of the soya milk.
Bake for 25 minutes until the pastry is puffed and golden. Serve with boiled green beans.

recipes.name: Lentil shepherd's pie
steps: Heat half the oil in a large pan and cook the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms for 10 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato purée and thyme for 1 minute, then add the lentils, tomatoes, stock and soy sauce. Simmer for 15–20 minutes until thick, then stir in the peas and season.
Meanwhile peel and chunk both kinds of potato and boil for 15 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with the soya milk, the rest of the oil and some seasoning. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Spoon the lentil mix into a 2-litre ovenproof dish and top with the mash, roughing it up with a fork.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is golden at the edges.

recipes.name: Oven-baked fish and chips with crushed peas
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with 20ml oil and a pinch of salt on a large baking tray and roast for 40 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp.
Pat the fish dry. Put the flour, beaten egg and panko mixed with the lemon zest in three shallow bowls. Dip each fillet in flour, then egg, then press into the crumbs.
Lay the fish on a second oiled tray, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for the last 15–18 minutes of the chips' cooking time until golden and the fish flakes easily.
Meanwhile cook the peas for 3 minutes, drain and roughly crush with the butter, mint and some seasoning.
Serve the fish and chips with the crushed peas and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Honey-mustard salmon traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the potatoes with half the oil and some seasoning in a large roasting tin and roast for 20 minutes.
Mix the honey, mustard, lemon zest and half the lemon juice.
Push the potatoes to the sides, add the broccoli and beans, drizzle with the rest of the oil and nestle in the salmon, skin side down.
Spoon the honey-mustard over the salmon and roast for 12–15 minutes until the salmon flakes easily.
Squeeze over the rest of the lemon juice and serve.

recipes.name: Smoked haddock kedgeree
steps: Put the haddock in a frying pan with the bay leaf, cover with 600ml water and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Lift out the fish, keep the water and flake the fish into large pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and quarter.
Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute, then the rice.
Pour in 600ml of the fish water (top up with boiling water if needed), cover and simmer very gently for 10 minutes. Add the peas, cover again and leave off the heat for 5 minutes.
Fork through the rice, fold in the haddock and parsley, and top with the eggs. Serve with lemon wedges and black pepper.

recipes.name: Spaghetti bolognese
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the mince over a high heat for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock, oregano and bay. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until rich and thick. Season.
Ten minutes before the sauce is ready, cook the spaghetti in a large pan of salted boiling water according to the packet. Drain, keeping a mugful of the water.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening with a splash of pasta water, and serve with the Parmesan.

recipes.name: Beef lasagne
steps: Make the ragù: brown the mince in the oil in a large pan, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic and purée, then the tomatoes, stock and oregano. Simmer for 30 minutes until thick; season.
Make the white sauce: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick, then season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
In a deep ovenproof dish (about 30 x 20cm), layer a third of the ragù, a layer of lasagne sheets and a quarter of the white sauce. Repeat twice more, then finish with the remaining white sauce.
Scatter over the cheddar and Parmesan and bake for 40–45 minutes until golden and the pasta is tender when poked with a knife.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting, so it holds its shape.

recipes.name: Chicken cacciatore

ingredients.note: about 8 thighs, skin removed if you like

steps: Season the chicken. Heat the oil in a large lidded casserole and brown the chicken on both sides for 8 minutes, then lift out.
Add the onion, pepper and mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, stock and oregano, return the chicken and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and cooked through.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes for 15–20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the olives into the sauce and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. Scatter over the basil and serve with the potatoes.

recipes.name: Spaghetti carbonara

ingredients.note: finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps: Cook the spaghetti in a large pan of salted boiling water according to the packet.
Meanwhile fry the pancetta in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5–6 minutes until crisp and golden. Take off the heat.
Beat the eggs with the Parmesan and lots of black pepper in a bowl.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and tip it into the pancetta pan (off the heat). Toss well.
Pour in the egg mixture with a splash of pasta water and toss quickly until glossy and creamy – the heat of the pasta cooks the egg without scrambling. Serve straight away with extra Parmesan.

recipes.name: Mushroom risotto

ingredients.note: made up with 1.2 litres boiling water

steps: Soak the porcini in 150ml boiling water for 10 minutes, then chop them and add the soaking liquid (leaving any grit behind) to the stock. Keep the stock hot on a low heat.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan and fry the fresh mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden. Add the onion, garlic and porcini and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add a ladle of stock and stir until absorbed. Keep adding stock a ladle at a time, stirring often, for 18–20 minutes until the rice is creamy and just tender.
Take off the heat and beat in the rest of the butter, the cheese and a squeeze of lemon. Season.
Cover and rest for 2 minutes, then serve sprinkled with parsley.

recipes.name: Pasta alla norma
steps: Heat 45ml oil in a large frying pan and fry the aubergine over a medium-high heat for 10–12 minutes, turning often, until golden and soft. Season and set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, the garlic and chilli flakes to the pan and sizzle for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir the aubergine back in.
Meanwhile cook the penne in salted boiling water according to the packet. Drain, keeping a little water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and a splash of pasta water, then stir through most of the basil. Serve topped with the rest.

recipes.name: Prawn, chilli and garlic linguine
steps: Cook the linguine in a large pan of salted boiling water according to the packet.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large frying pan and gently fry the garlic and chilli for 1–2 minutes without letting the garlic brown.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until starting to soften, then add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink all the way through.
Drain the pasta, keeping a mugful of water, and toss it into the pan with the lemon zest and juice, parsley and a splash of pasta water until glossy. Season and serve.

recipes.name: Gnocchi bake with tomato and mozzarella
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Heat the oil in an ovenproof pan and fry the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until wilted and season.
Meanwhile boil the gnocchi for 2 minutes until they float, then drain and stir into the sauce with half the basil.
Tip into a baking dish if your pan isn't ovenproof, scatter over the mozzarella and hard cheese and bake for 12–15 minutes until bubbling and golden. Top with the rest of the basil.

recipes.name: Sausage ragù rigatoni
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the sausage meat over a medium-high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until browned.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic, fennel seeds, chilli flakes and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes plus half a tin of water and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water according to the packet, drain (keeping a little water) and stir into the sauce with a splash of the water.
Serve with the Parmesan.

recipes.name: Chicken tikka masala
steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt and 40g of the curry paste. Leave for at least 10 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Heat the grill to high (or the oven to 240°C (220°C fan)). Spread the chicken on a lined tray and grill for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, tomato purée and the rest of the paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 100ml water and simmer for 10 minutes. Cook the rice according to the packet.
Stir the cream, sugar, garam masala and the chicken into the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. Season, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Chickpea and spinach curry (chana saag)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and sizzle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the ground coriander, turmeric and garam masala for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and 150ml water and simmer for 15 minutes. Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted. Season with salt and the lemon juice and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Lamb rogan josh
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pan and fry the cardamom, bay and cinnamon for 30 seconds. Add the onions and cook for 12 minutes until deep golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then add the lamb and cook for 5 minutes until sealed all over.
Add the cumin, coriander, paprika and chilli powder, then stir in the yoghurt a spoonful at a time.
Add the tomatoes and 250ml water, cover and simmer very gently for 1¼–1½ hours until the lamb is tender. Add a splash of water if it catches.
Cook the rice according to the packet. Stir the garam masala into the curry, season and scatter with coriander.

recipes.name: Tarka dal
steps: Put the lentils, turmeric, ginger and 1 litre of water in a pan. Bring to the boil, skim off any foam and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes and simmer for 5 more minutes until thick but pourable. Season with salt. Cook the rice according to the packet.
For the tarka, heat the oil in a small frying pan and sizzle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then add the onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute.
Pour the sizzling tarka over the dal, sprinkle with garam masala, lemon juice and coriander, and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Chicken korma
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the cardamom for 30 seconds. Add the onions and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft but not brown.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the coriander, cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, then add the ground almonds and 200ml water. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Stir in the yoghurt, cream, sugar and garam masala and heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling. Season and serve scattered with coriander.

recipes.name: Paneer and pea curry (matar paneer)
steps: Heat half the oil in a large non-stick pan and fry the paneer for 5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and the cumin seeds, then the onion, and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute, then the ground spices for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and 200ml water and simmer for 10 minutes. Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Add the peas and paneer and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the garam masala, season and serve with coriander and the rice.

recipes.name: Keralan coconut fish curry
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seeds. When they pop (about 30 seconds), add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies for 1 minute, then the turmeric, coriander and chilli powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes. Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Lower the fish into the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 5–6 minutes until it flakes easily – don't stir too much or it will break up.
Season with salt and lime juice, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Sweet and sour chicken
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Mix the pineapple juice with the ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and 10g cornflour to make the sauce.
Toss the chicken in the remaining cornflour. Heat 30ml oil in a wok or large frying pan and fry the chicken over a high heat for 6–7 minutes until golden and cooked through. Lift out.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the onion and peppers for 3 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes until thick and glossy. Return the chicken with the pineapple and toss for 1 minute.
Scatter with spring onions and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Beef and broccoli stir-fry
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Toss the beef with the cornflour and 15ml soy sauce.
Mix the rest of the soy sauce with the oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil and 60ml water.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot and stir-fry the beef in two batches for 1–2 minutes each until browned. Lift out.
Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, add the broccoli, beef and sauce and toss for 1–2 minutes until glossy. Serve over the rice with spring onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Hoisin pork noodles
steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet, drain and toss with the sesame oil.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and fry the pork over a high heat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and slightly crisp.
Add the garlic, ginger and pepper and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the pak choi and cook for 2 minutes more.
Stir in the hoisin, soy sauce and 2 tbsp water, then add the noodles and toss until coated and hot. Serve with spring onions and chilli flakes.

recipes.name: Mushroom mapo tofu
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the mushrooms over a high heat for 6–8 minutes until browned and crumbly, like mince.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilli bean paste and chilli flakes and stir-fry for 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, then gently slide in the tofu. Simmer for 5 minutes without stirring too much, so the tofu stays whole.
Stir in the cornflour mix and simmer for 1 minute until glossy. Drizzle with sesame oil, scatter with spring onions and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Kung pao chicken
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Toss the chicken with the cornflour and 15ml soy sauce.
Mix the rest of the soy sauce with the vinegar, sugar and 3 tbsp water.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot and stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add the chilli flakes, garlic, ginger and pepper and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1 minute until sticky, then toss in the spring onions and peanuts. Serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Thai green chicken curry
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan and fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat for 2 minutes, then pour in the coconut milk and 100ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes until just tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Season with the fish sauce, sugar and lime juice, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Prawn pad Thai
steps: Soak the noodles in just-boiled water for 5–8 minutes (or as the packet says) until just soft, then drain and rinse in cold water.
Mix the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok over a high heat. Fry the garlic for 20 seconds, add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Push to one side, pour in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds, then add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the beansprouts and spring onions and toss for 1 minute until the sprouts are hot. Serve topped with peanuts, chilli flakes, coriander and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Thai red vegetable curry

ingredients.note: or soy sauce if gluten isn't a concern

steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato, coconut milk and 200ml water and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the pepper and chickpeas and simmer for 5–6 minutes until the sweet potato is tender. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Season with the tamari, sugar and lime juice, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Thai basil pork with fried egg (pad kra pao)
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Mix the oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp water.
Heat 15ml oil in a wok over a high heat and fry the garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Add the pork and stir-fry for 6–7 minutes until browned and cooked through, then add the beans for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce, toss for 1 minute, then stir through the basil until wilted.
In a frying pan, fry the eggs in the remaining oil over a high heat until the edges are crisp. Serve the pork on rice with an egg on top.

recipes.name: Chicken katsu curry
steps: For the sauce, heat 15ml oil in a pan and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and 15g flour and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the stock, add the soy and honey and simmer for 15 minutes. Blend until smooth (or leave chunky).
Cook the rice according to the packet. Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).
Season the chicken. Dip each piece in flour, then beaten egg, then panko, pressing it on well.

Heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan and fry the chicken for 2 minutes each side until golden, then transfer to a tray and bake for 10–12 minutes until cooked through (or air-fry at 200°C for 12–14 minutes).
Slice the chicken and serve on the rice with the curry sauce poured alongside.

recipes.name: Teriyaki salmon with rice and greens
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Mix the soy sauce, mirin, honey and ginger.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes until crisp, then turn and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 1–2 minutes, spooning it over the salmon until sticky and the fish is cooked through.
Meanwhile steam or boil the broccoli for 4 minutes.
Serve the salmon on the rice with the broccoli, spoon over the glaze and scatter with sesame seeds and spring onions.

recipes.name: Miso-glazed aubergine with edamame rice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Score the cut side of the aubergines in a criss-cross pattern, brush with the vegetable oil and roast cut side up for 25 minutes until soft.
Mix the miso, mirin, maple syrup and sesame oil into a paste.
Cook the rice according to the packet, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Spread the miso glaze over the aubergines and return to the oven for 8–10 minutes until bubbling and caramelised.
Steam the pak choi for 3 minutes. Serve the aubergine on the rice with the pak choi, sprinkled with sesame seeds and spring onions.

recipes.name: Chilli con carne
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the mince for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes, then the garlic, spices, oregano and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock, bring to a simmer and cook gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the kidney beans and simmer for 10 minutes more until thick. Season. Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Serve the chilli on the rice with a spoonful of soured cream.

recipes.name: Chicken fajitas
steps: Toss the chicken with the paprika, cumin, chilli, garlic, the juice of 1 lime, half the oil and a pinch of salt.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and cook the peppers and onion for 5 minutes until charred at the edges. Push to the side.
Add the chicken and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until golden and cooked through.
Mash the avocado with the juice of the other lime and a pinch of salt. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or the microwave.
Serve everything at the table so everyone can fill their own wraps with chicken, veg, guacamole, soured cream, cheese and lettuce.

recipes.name: Black bean and sweet potato enchiladas
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the sweet potato with half the oil and roast for 20 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile heat the rest of the oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Mix the passata with the chipotle paste and a pinch of salt. Stir the beans, roasted sweet potato and a third of the sauce into the onion mix.
Spread a little sauce in a large baking dish. Fill each tortilla with the bean mix, roll up and lay seam-side down in the dish.
Pour over the rest of the sauce, scatter with the cheese and bake for 20 minutes until bubbling. Serve with soured cream and coriander.

recipes.name: Pulled pork tacos
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Rub the pork all over with the paprika, cumin, sugar and salt.
Put the onion and garlic in a lidded casserole, sit the pork on top and add 150ml water. Cover and cook for 3½ hours until it falls apart (or slow-cook on low for 8 hours).
Meanwhile toss the red onion with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt and leave to quick-pickle. Toss the cabbage with the juice of the other lime.
Lift out the pork and shred it with two forks, discarding any fat. Skim the fat from the juices and stir 100ml of them into the pork with the BBQ sauce.
Warm the tortillas and serve filled with the pork, cabbage, pickled onion and coriander.

recipes.name: Crispy fish tacos with lime slaw
steps: Toss the fish with the spices, oil and a pinch of salt.
Toss the cabbage with the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Mix the mayonnaise with the chipotle paste and a squeeze of lime.
Heat a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the fish for 2–3 minutes each side until golden and flaking.
Warm the tortillas, then fill with slaw, fish, avocado, chipotle mayo and coriander. Serve with the remaining lime in wedges.

recipes.name: Three-bean chilli
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, spices, oregano and tomato purée and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and all the beans. Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Season.
Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Serve the chilli on the rice topped with avocado and coriander, with lime wedges to squeeze over.

recipes.name: Shakshuka
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan with a lid and cook the onion and peppers for 10 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Season.
Make 8 dips in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on a low heat for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Scatter with feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Chicken shawarma traybake

ingredients.note: 150g for the marinade, 150g for the sauce

steps: Mix 150g yoghurt with the spices, two-thirds of the garlic, the lemon zest, half the juice, half the oil and the salt. Coat the chicken (leave for 30 minutes if you have time).
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Spread the chicken, onion and pepper on a large roasting tray and drizzle with the rest of the oil.
Roast for 25–30 minutes until the chicken is charred at the edges and cooked through.
Mix the remaining yoghurt with the tahini, the rest of the garlic and lemon juice and a splash of water to make a drizzling sauce.
Slice the chicken and serve in warm pittas with the onions, peppers, cucumber, tomatoes and tahini yoghurt.

recipes.name: Lamb kofta flatbreads
steps: Mix the lamb with the grated onion, half the garlic, the spices, half the herbs and the salt. Shape into 12 sausage shapes.
Toss the sliced onion with half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and leave to soften.
Mix the yoghurt with the cucumber, the rest of the garlic and mint, and a squeeze of lemon.
Heat the grill to high (or a griddle pan). Brush the kofta with oil and grill for 10–12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads and fill with the kofta, tomatoes, pickled onion, yoghurt and the rest of the parsley.

recipes.name: Baked falafel bowls with tahini dressing
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Blitz the chickpeas, onion, garlic, spices, parsley, flour and salt in a food processor until finely chopped but not a paste.
Shape into 20 small patties, lay on an oiled baking tray, brush with 30ml oil and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile put the couscous in a bowl with a pinch of salt, pour over 300ml boiling water, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir in the remaining oil.
Whisk the tahini with the juice of the lemon and 4–5 tbsp cold water until smooth and pourable.
Serve the falafel on the couscous with cucumber and tomatoes, drizzled with the tahini dressing.

recipes.name: Moussaka
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush the aubergine slices with most of the oil, lay on trays with the potato slices and roast for 20 minutes until soft and golden.
Meanwhile brown the lamb in a large pan for 6 minutes, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic, cinnamon and oregano. Stir in the purée and tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes. Season.

For the topping, melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute and gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick, cool slightly, then beat in the egg, half the cheese and the nutmeg.
Layer the potatoes in a large baking dish, then half the aubergine, all the lamb, and the rest of the aubergine. Pour over the sauce and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Turn the oven down to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for 40–45 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

recipes.name: Halloumi and roast vegetable traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the peppers, courgettes, onions, tomatoes and chickpeas with 30ml oil, the oregano and pepper on a large roasting tray.
Roast for 25 minutes until the veg is soft and starting to char.
Lay the halloumi slices on top, drizzle with the honey and remaining oil and roast for 10–12 minutes more until golden.
Meanwhile put the couscous in a bowl, pour over 250ml boiling water, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff up with the lemon zest and juice.
Serve the traybake on the couscous scattered with mint.

recipes.name: Baked cod with tomatoes, olives and butter beans
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Heat the oil in a large ovenproof frying pan or shallow casserole and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, olives, oregano and 100ml water and simmer for 5 minutes until the tomatoes start to burst. Stir in the spinach to wilt.
Season the cod and nestle it into the beans. Squeeze over half the lemon.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Scatter with parsley and serve with the rest of the lemon in wedges.

recipes.name: Greek baked butter beans (gigantes plaki)
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Heat half the oil in a flameproof dish and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and purée for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, sugar and 200ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes and season.
Stir in the beans, drizzle with the rest of the oil and bake uncovered for 35–40 minutes until thick and slightly crusty on top.
Scatter with parsley and serve warm with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Chicken and chorizo paella
steps: Heat the oil in a large, wide frying pan or paella pan and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Add the chorizo and cook for 2 minutes until it releases its oil.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic, paprika and turmeric for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice to coat, then add the tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 18–20 minutes without stirring, until the rice is just tender and most of the liquid has gone.
Scatter over the peas, cover with a lid or foil and cook for 5 minutes more.
Rest for 5 minutes, then scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Chorizo and butter bean stew
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the chorizo for 3–4 minutes until crisp and its red oil runs out.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 6 minutes, then the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer for 12 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, season with pepper and serve with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Jerk chicken with rice and peas
steps: Slash the chicken a few times and rub all over with the jerk paste, lime juice and oil. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the chicken on a rack over a tray for 40–45 minutes until charred and cooked through (75°C at the bone).
Meanwhile put the rice, beans, coconut milk, 250ml water, half the spring onions, the garlic, thyme and salt in a lidded pan. Bring to the boil.
Cover, turn the heat right down and cook for 15 minutes, then leave off the heat with the lid on for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Serve the chicken with the rice and peas, scattered with the remaining spring onions.

recipes.name: Caribbean sweet potato and chickpea curry
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, chilli, curry powder and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, chickpeas, tomatoes, coconut milk and 150ml water. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then season with salt and the lime juice. Serve with the rice, topped with spring onions.

recipes.name: Beef bulgogi rice bowls
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and gochujang. Toss the beef in it and leave for 15 minutes while you cook the rice according to the packet.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over a very high heat.
Add the beef in two batches, letting excess marinade drip off, and fry for 2–3 minutes until caramelised. Add any leftover marinade at the end and bubble for 30 seconds.
Serve the beef over the rice with the carrot, cucumber and kimchi, scattered with spring onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Crispy tofu bibimbap
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet. Mix the gochujang, honey, vinegar and 10ml sesame oil into a sauce.
Toss the tofu in the cornflour. Heat 20ml oil in a large non-stick frying pan and fry for 8–10 minutes, turning, until crisp all over. Toss with 15ml soy sauce and set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry the carrots and courgette for 3 minutes; set aside. Stir-fry the spinach and beansprouts with the garlic and the rest of the soy sauce for 2 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set and the yolks runny.
Divide the rice between bowls, arrange the veg and tofu on top, add an egg and drizzle with the gochujang sauce, remaining sesame oil and sesame seeds. Mix everything together to eat.

recipes.name: Smash burgers with oven chips
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and bake the oven chips for the time on the packet (usually 20–25 minutes), turning once.
Divide the mince into 8 loose balls. Mix the ketchup, mayo and mustard to make a burger sauce. Toast the cut sides of the buns in a dry pan.
Heat a large heavy frying pan until very hot and add a little oil. Add 2–3 balls with a few onion slices on each and smash flat with a spatula. Season and cook for 2 minutes until crusty.
Flip, top with cheese and cook for 1 minute more until cooked through. Repeat with the rest.
Spread the buns with sauce and stack two patties in each with lettuce and gherkins. Serve with the chips.

recipes.name: Macaroni cheese with broccoli
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet says, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Drain.
Melt the butter in the pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until thick and smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in the mustard, nutmeg and three-quarters of the cheese until melted. Season.
Stir in the pasta and broccoli, tip into a baking dish and scatter with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

recipes.name: Air-fryer crispy chicken tenders with slaw and wedges
steps: Toss the sweet potato wedges with half the oil and a pinch of salt and air-fry at 200°C for 18–20 minutes, shaking halfway. Keep warm.
Season the flour with the paprika, salt and pepper. Dip the chicken strips in the flour, then the egg, then the panko.
Spray or brush the tenders with the rest of the oil and air-fry in a single layer at 200°C for 10–12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through (in batches if needed).
Mix the cabbage and carrot with the mayonnaise and lemon juice and season.
Serve the tenders with the wedges and slaw.

recipes.name: Chicken, chorizo and prawn jambalaya
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded pan and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Add the chorizo for 2 minutes.
Add the onion, celery and pepper and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic and Cajun seasoning for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently for 18 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Stir in the prawns, cover and cook for 4–5 minutes until they are pink and the rice is tender.
Scatter with spring onions and serve.

recipes.name: Spanish tortilla with salad
steps: Heat the oil in a 24cm non-stick frying pan and gently cook the potatoes and onion over a low heat for 20 minutes, turning now and then, until tender but not browned.
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl. Lift the potatoes out with a slotted spoon, stir into the eggs and leave for 5 minutes. Pour off all but 15ml of the oil.
Pour the mixture back into the pan and cook over a low heat for 8 minutes until almost set.
Slide onto a plate, flip back into the pan and cook for 3 more minutes. Serve warm or cold in wedges, with little gem leaves.

recipes.name: Minestrone soup

ingredients.note: made up with 1 litre boiling water

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, courgette and tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock and oregano, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and simmer for 8–10 minutes until tender. Stir in the spinach to wilt, season and serve.

recipes.name: Tomato and red lentil soup
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes until softening.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock, bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Blend until smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick. Season and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Caesar wraps
steps: Toss the chicken and lettuce with the dressing, half the Parmesan and some black pepper.
Warm the tortillas for 10 seconds in the microwave so they fold without cracking.
Divide the filling between the wraps, sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Cut in half on the diagonal to serve, or wrap in foil to take to work.

recipes.name: Tuna niçoise salad
steps: Boil the potatoes for 12–15 minutes until tender, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes. Drain and cool.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 7–8 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and mustard with the salt and pepper.
Arrange the lettuce, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, olives, tuna and eggs on plates or in lunchboxes and drizzle with the dressing.

recipes.name: Halloumi and houmous wraps
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the halloumi for 1–2 minutes each side until golden.
Spread each tortilla with houmous.
Top with spinach, pepper, cucumber and the hot halloumi, then sprinkle with chilli flakes.
Roll up tightly and cut in half to serve.

recipes.name: Kimchi fried rice with fried egg

ingredients.note: chopped, plus 2 tbsp of its juice

steps: If not using leftovers, cook the rice according to the packet, spread on a tray and let it cool and steam dry for 10 minutes.
Heat 15ml oil in a wok over a high heat and stir-fry the kimchi and most of the spring onions for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, peas, gochujang, soy sauce and kimchi juice and stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until piping hot. Stir in the sesame oil.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil and serve on the rice with the remaining spring onions.

recipes.name: Smoked mackerel, beetroot and potato salad
steps: Boil the potatoes for 12–15 minutes until tender, drain and leave to cool slightly.
Mix the crème fraîche with the mustard, the juice of half the lemon and plenty of pepper.
Toss the warm potatoes with half the dressing and the red onion.
Arrange the spinach, potatoes, beetroot and mackerel on plates, drizzle with the rest of the dressing and scatter with parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Ginger chicken noodle soup

ingredients.note: made up with 1.2 litres boiling water

steps: Bring the stock, ginger and garlic to a simmer in a large pan. Add the chicken and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred with two forks.
Add the soy sauce and noodles to the broth and cook for 4 minutes, adding the pak choi and sweetcorn for the last 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, then ladle into bowls and top with spring onions, chilli and a few drops of sesame oil.

recipes.name: Leek and potato soup

ingredients.note: made up with 1 litre boiling water

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the leeks and onion gently with a lid on for 10 minutes until soft but not brown.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the potatoes and stock.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Blend until smooth (or leave chunky), season well with black pepper and serve.

recipes.name: Chickpea, feta and herb couscous salad
steps: Put the couscous and cumin in a large bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff up with a fork and leave to cool for a few minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, herbs, lemon zest and juice and olive oil.
Crumble over the feta and serve, or pack into lunchboxes (keeps for 2 days in the fridge).

recipes.name: Ham, pea and cheddar frittata
steps: Heat the grill to high. Beat the eggs with the milk, most of the cheese and plenty of pepper.
Heat the oil in a 24cm ovenproof non-stick frying pan and soften the spring onions for 2 minutes. Add the peas and ham.
Pour in the eggs and cook over a low-medium heat for 6–8 minutes, without stirring, until the bottom is set.
Scatter with the rest of the cheese and grill for 3–4 minutes until puffed and golden. Cut into wedges; serve warm or cold.

recipes.name: Cheese, bean and sweetcorn quesadillas
steps: Mix the beans, sweetcorn, spring onions and paprika.
Spread over 4 tortillas, scatter with cheese and top with the remaining tortillas, pressing down.
Cook one at a time in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 2 minutes each side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with soured cream.

recipes.name: Satay noodle salad
steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet, then rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, lime juice, sugar, ginger and sesame oil with 3–4 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the pepper, carrot, cucumber, cabbage, spring onions and the dressing.
Serve topped with peanuts, coriander and chilli flakes.

recipes.name: Black bean burrito bowls
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet, then stir in the juice of 1 lime and half the coriander.
Heat the oil in a pan, add the spices for 30 seconds, then the beans and 3 tbsp water and warm through for 3 minutes. Season.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, the rest of the coriander and a squeeze of lime to make a quick salsa.
Build bowls with lettuce, rice, beans, sweetcorn, avocado and salsa, with the last lime in wedges.

recipes.name: Berry overnight oats
steps: Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt, chia seeds and honey in a bowl or divide between 4 jars.
Spoon the frozen berries on top – they defrost overnight and make a quick compote.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Stir and eat cold, adding a splash more milk if it's too thick. Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Peanut butter and banana overnight oats
steps: Whisk the peanut butter, maple syrup and cinnamon into the soya milk until smooth.
Stir in the oats and chia seeds and divide between 4 jars or bowls.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Top with sliced banana just before eating.

recipes.name: Apple and cinnamon porridge
steps: Put the oats, milk, 300ml water, cinnamon and half the grated apple in a pan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Add a splash more water or milk if you like it looser.
Spoon into bowls and top with the rest of the apple, the seeds and a drizzle of honey.

recipes.name: Berry and banana smoothie
steps: Peel and break the bananas into a blender.
Add the frozen berries, soya milk, chia seeds and maple syrup.
Blend for 1–2 minutes until completely smooth, adding a splash of water if too thick.
Pour into glasses and drink straight away.

recipes.name: Greek yoghurt bowls with berries, honey and seeds
steps: Divide the yoghurt between 4 bowls.
Top with the blueberries.
Scatter over the seeds.
Drizzle with honey and serve.

recipes.name: Scrambled eggs on toast
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Put the bread in the toaster.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over a low heat, add the eggs and stir gently with a spatula for 3–4 minutes until softly set. Take off the heat while still a little runny – they keep cooking.
Pile onto the hot toast and scatter with chives.

recipes.name: Smashed avocado on sourdough
steps: Toast the sourdough.
Mash the avocado flesh with the lime juice and salt with a fork, leaving it a little chunky.
Spread over the toast and top with the tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

recipes.name: Freezable breakfast burritos
steps: Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan and cook the pepper and spring onions for 4 minutes. Add the paprika and beans and warm through for 2 minutes.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over a low heat for 3–4 minutes until just set. Season.
Warm the tortillas, divide the filling between them, scatter with cheese and roll up tightly, tucking in the ends.
Eat straight away, or cool, wrap each in foil and freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat from frozen in foil at 200°C (180°C fan) for 25 minutes, or unwrapped in the microwave for 2–3 minutes.

recipes.name: Full English breakfast
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roast the sausages on a tray for 25 minutes, turning once; add the tomatoes, cut side up, for the last 15 minutes.
Meanwhile fry the bacon in a large frying pan for 3–4 minutes each side until crisp, then move it to the oven tray to keep warm. Fry the black pudding for 2 minutes each side and add it too.
Fry the mushrooms in the bacon fat with half the butter for 5 minutes until golden. Warm the beans in a small pan.
Wipe the pan, add the oil and fry the eggs for 3–4 minutes until the whites are set. Toast and butter the bread.
Share everything between 4 warm plates and serve straight away.

recipes.name: Veggie full English breakfast
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the vegetarian sausages on a tray for the time on the packet (usually 15–20 minutes), adding the tomatoes for the last 15 minutes.
Fry the mushrooms in half the butter for 5 minutes until golden; keep warm. Warm the beans in a small pan.
Dry-fry the halloumi in a hot pan for 1–2 minutes each side until golden.
Add the oil to the pan and fry the eggs for 3–4 minutes. Toast the bread and spread with the rest of the butter.
Share everything between 4 warm plates and serve.

recipes.name: Fluffy American pancakes with blueberries

ingredients.note: melted, plus a little for the pan

steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl. Whisk the eggs, milk and 20g melted butter in a jug.
Pour the wet mix into the dry and whisk briefly until just combined – a few lumps are fine.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and brush with butter. Add 2 tbsp batter per pancake, dot with a few blueberries and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear.
Flip and cook for 1 minute more until golden. Keep warm while you make the rest (about 12).
Serve stacked with the remaining blueberries and maple syrup.

recipes.name: Crêpes with lemon and sugar
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, half the melted butter and the salt into a smooth batter the thickness of single cream. Rest for 10 minutes if you have time.
Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat and wipe with a little melted butter.
Pour in a small ladleful of batter and swirl to coat the base thinly. Cook for 1 minute until golden underneath, then flip and cook for 30 seconds.
Repeat to make about 8 crêpes, stacking them on a warm plate.
Serve sprinkled with sugar and a good squeeze of lemon, folded into quarters.

recipes.name: Green shakshuka with feta
steps: Heat the oil in a large lidded frying pan and cook the leeks and courgette for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute, then stir in the spinach until wilted. Season.
Make 8 hollows and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on a low heat for 6–8 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
Spoon over the yoghurt, scatter with feta, chilli flakes and parsley and serve from the pan.

recipes.name: Eggs royale

ingredients.note: 4 for poaching, 3 yolks for the hollandaise

steps: For the hollandaise, melt the butter. Whisk 3 egg yolks with 1 tbsp lemon juice in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water until thick and pale.
Take off the heat and slowly whisk in the melted butter, a little at a time, until thick and glossy. Season with lemon and pepper and keep warm.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack in the 4 eggs one at a time and poach for 3 minutes, then lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toast the muffins and top each half with smoked salmon.
Add a poached egg to each, spoon over the hollandaise and finish with black pepper.

recipes.name: French toast with warm berries
steps: Warm the berries in a small pan for 5 minutes until juicy.
Whisk the eggs, milk and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Melt a little butter in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Dip the brioche in the egg for a few seconds each side and fry for 2 minutes each side until golden. Repeat with the rest.
Serve topped with the berries, a spoonful of yoghurt and a drizzle of maple syrup.

recipes.name: Smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels
steps: Toast the bagels.
Spread generously with cream cheese.
Top with the smoked salmon, a few slices of red onion and the chives.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and plenty of black pepper.

recipes.name: Chorizo and potato breakfast hash
steps: Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes until just tender, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry the chorizo for 3 minutes until it releases its oil. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and paprika and fry for 10 minutes, turning now and then, until crisp. Season.
Make 4 hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4–5 minutes until the whites are set. Scatter with parsley.

recipes.name: Huevos rancheros
steps: Heat half the oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, chilli and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Season with salt and a squeeze of lime.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds each side; keep wrapped in a tea towel.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Put 2 tortillas on each plate, spoon over the beans, top with an egg, avocado and coriander, and serve with lime wedges.

recipes.name: Turkish eggs (çılbır)
steps: Mix the yoghurt with the garlic and salt and let it come to room temperature. Spread over 4 plates.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar and poach the eggs, 4 at a time, for 3 minutes. Drain on kitchen paper.
Melt the butter in a small pan until foaming, then take off the heat and stir in the chilli flakes.
Sit 2 eggs on each plate of yoghurt, spoon over the chilli butter, scatter with mint and serve with toast.

recipes.name: Grilled kippers with buttered toast
steps: Heat the grill to high. Lay the kippers skin side up on a foil-lined tray with the tomatoes, cut side up.
Grill for 4–5 minutes until the kippers are hot through and the tomatoes soft. (Or jug them: stand in a jug of just-boiled water for 5 minutes.)
Meanwhile toast the bread and spread with most of the butter.
Serve the kippers with a small knob of butter melting on top, the tomatoes, toast, lemon wedges and black pepper.

recipes.name: Tofu scramble on sourdough
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the spring onions and garlic for 2 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu with your hands, add the turmeric, paprika and salt and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until hot and lightly golden.
Add the tomatoes and spinach and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Season with pepper.
Toast the sourdough and pile the scramble on top.

recipes.name: Welsh rarebit with tomato salad
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk until thick.
Off the heat, stir in the cheese, mustard, paprika and pepper until you have a thick paste. (A dash of Worcestershire sauce is traditional but not vegetarian.)
Heat the grill to high and toast the bread on one side. Spread the cheese mix over the untoasted sides, right to the edges.
Grill for 3–4 minutes until bubbling and golden-brown in patches. Serve with the tomatoes and little gem leaves.

recipes.name: Ploughman's lunch
steps: Take the cheese out of the fridge 20 minutes before serving so it has more flavour.
Slice the bread and put it on a board with the butter.
Arrange the cheese, pickle, apple, celery, tomatoes and lettuce on plates or a big board.
Let everyone help themselves.

recipes.name: Roast tomato soup with cheese toasties
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes. Add most of the basil and blend until smooth. Season.
Meanwhile butter the bread on one side. Make 4 sandwiches with the cheese inside and the butter outside.
Cook the toasties in a large frying pan over a medium heat for 3 minutes each side until golden and melted.
Serve the soup topped with the rest of the basil, with the toasties cut into soldiers for dunking.

recipes.name: Miso chicken ramen

ingredients.note: made up with 1.5 litres boiling water

steps: Simmer the stock with the ginger and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the chicken and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked through, then lift out and slice.
Meanwhile boil the eggs for 6½ minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve – the yolks will be jammy.
Whisk the miso and soy sauce into the broth (don't let it boil hard after adding the miso).
Cook the noodles according to the packet, adding the pak choi for the last 2 minutes. Drain and divide between bowls.
Ladle over the broth and top with chicken, eggs, sweetcorn, spring onions, sesame oil and chilli flakes.

recipes.name: Jacket potatoes with beans and cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Prick the potatoes all over with a fork.

Microwave on high for 8–10 minutes until they give when squeezed, then rub with salt and bake directly on the oven shelf for 20 minutes until the skins are crisp. (Or bake for 1–1¼ hours without microwaving.)
Meanwhile warm the beans in a small pan.
Split the potatoes, add a knob of butter, spoon over the beans and top with the cheese.

recipes.name: Falafel wraps with houmous and slaw
steps: Heat the falafel according to the packet instructions.
Toss the cabbage with the juice of half the lemon and a pinch of chilli flakes.
Warm the tortillas and spread each with houmous.
Fill with falafel, slaw, cucumber and tomatoes, squeeze over more lemon, roll up and cut in half.

recipes.name: Greek salad with warm pitta

ingredients.note: in one block or thick slices

steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, onion, pepper and olives in a large bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar and salt and toss through the salad.
Lay the feta on top and sprinkle with oregano.
Warm the pittas in the toaster and serve alongside.

recipes.name: Chicken, bacon and avocado club sandwich
steps: Grill or fry the bacon for 3–4 minutes each side until crisp.
Toast the bread and spread each slice thinly with mayonnaise.
For each sandwich, layer a slice of toast with chicken and lettuce, add a second slice, then bacon, avocado and tomato, and top with a third slice.
Push in 4 cocktail sticks, cut into triangles and serve.

recipes.name: Spiced butternut squash soup with crusty bread

ingredients.note: made up with 1 litre boiling water

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the squash and onion with the oil, cumin and chilli on a roasting tray and roast for 30 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges.
Tip into a large pan with the garlic and the stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until smooth, adding a little water if too thick. Season with pepper.
Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Creamy garlic mushrooms on toast
steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the mushrooms for 6–8 minutes until golden and any liquid has gone.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the crème fraîche and lemon juice and bubble for 1 minute. Season.
Meanwhile toast the bread.
Spoon the mushrooms over the toast and scatter with parsley.

recipes.name: Tuna, sweetcorn and pepper pasta salad
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet, then drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Mix the mayonnaise, yoghurt and lemon juice with some seasoning.
Toss the pasta with the dressing, tuna, sweetcorn, pepper and spring onions.
Serve straight away or chill in lunchboxes for up to 2 days.

sesame-seeds.qualityNotes: Own-label is as good as brands for this.

sliced-bread.name: Wholemeal sliced bread
sliced-bread.qualityNotes: Medium-sliced 800g loaf (about 20 slices, ~40g each). Some loaves contain soya flour.

smoked-haddock.name: Smoked haddock fillets
smoked-haddock.qualityNotes: Undyed (pale) rather than bright yellow dyed; MSC-certified.

smoked-mackerel.name: Smoked mackerel fillets
smoked-mackerel.qualityNotes: Plain or peppered fillets from the chilled fish counter/aisle.

smoked-paprika.name: Smoked paprika
smoked-paprika.qualityNotes: Spanish pimentón (sweet/dulce) has the best flavour.

smoked-salmon.name: Smoked salmon
smoked-salmon.qualityNotes: Scottish smoked salmon; 'trimmings' packs are much cheaper for scrambled eggs and bagels.

sour-cream.name: Soured cream
sour-cream.qualityNotes: Own-label is fine; check the use-by date.

soy-sauce.name: Light soy sauce
soy-sauce.qualityNotes: Naturally brewed (Kikkoman, Lee Kum Kee, Pearl River Bridge) is a real step up from cheap blended soy sauces.

soya-milk.name: Unsweetened soya milk
soya-milk.qualityNotes: Unsweetened UHT; long-life cartons are in the ambient aisle.

spaghetti.name: Spaghetti
spaghetti.qualityNotes: Bronze-die Italian pasta (De Cecco, own-label 'finest') holds sauce better, but standard own-label is perfectly good.

spring-onions.name: Spring onions
spring-onions.qualityNotes: Sold as a bunch of about 8.

sushi-rice.name: Sushi rice
sushi-rice.qualityNotes: Japanese short-grain; slightly sticky, right for katsu, teriyaki and bibimbap bowls.

sweet-potatoes.name: Sweet potatoes
sweet-potatoes.qualityNotes: Firm, unblemished, not sprouting; loose is usually cheaper per kg than pre-packed.

sweetcorn.name: Sweetcorn in water
sweetcorn.qualityNotes: Small 198g tins (about 165g drained), no added sugar or salt.

tahini.name: Tahini
tahini.qualityNotes: Lebanese/Middle Eastern brands (e.g. Al Yaman) are smoother and cheaper per gram than health-food brands.

thai-green-curry-paste.name: Thai green curry paste
thai-green-curry-paste.qualityNotes: Mae Ploy or Thai Taste beat most own-label pastes. Many contain shrimp paste (Mae Ploy does); Thai Taste is vegan.

thai-red-curry-paste-vegan.name: Thai red curry paste vegan
thai-red-curry-paste-vegan.qualityNotes: Thai Taste red curry paste is vegan and authentic; many others contain shrimp paste – check the label.

tikka-curry-paste.name: Tikka masala curry paste
tikka-curry-paste.qualityNotes: Patak's is the benchmark and noticeably better than most own-label pastes.

tofu-firm.name: Extra firm tofu
tofu-firm.qualityNotes: Chilled extra-firm block (e.g. Tofoo, Cauldron); press out water before frying for crispness.

tomato-ketchup.name: Tomato ketchup
tomato-ketchup.qualityNotes: Heinz is genuinely the favourite; contains celery in its spice extracts.

tomato-puree.name: Tomato purée
tomato-puree.qualityNotes: Double concentrated, in a tube so it keeps after opening.

tuna-chunks.name: Tuna chunks in spring water

tuna-chunks.qualityNotes: Pole-and-line or MSC; 145g tin (about 102g drained). Brands aren't meaningfully better.

vegetable-oil.name: Vegetable oil
vegetable-oil.qualityNotes: Rapeseed or sunflower; own-label is the same product.

vegetable-stock-cube.name: Vegetable stock cubes
vegetable-stock-cube.qualityNotes: Gluten-free cubes (e.g. Kallo) so recipes stay gluten-free. Most contain celery.

vegetarian-hard-cheese.name: Vegetarian Italian hard cheese
vegetarian-hard-cheese.qualityNotes: Italian-style hard cheese made with vegetarian rennet. Many contain lysozyme (egg) – hence the egg allergen.

vegetarian-sausages.name: Vegetarian sausages
vegetarian-sausages.qualityNotes: Quorn and Linda McCartney vary; check for egg if vegan.

vine-tomatoes.name: Vine tomatoes
vine-tomatoes.qualityNotes: Firm, unblemished, not sprouting; loose is usually cheaper per kg than pre-packed.

white-miso.name: White miso paste
white-miso.qualityNotes: Shiro (white) miso; some misos contain barley – check if gluten matters.

worcestershire-sauce.name: Worcestershire sauce
worcestershire-sauce.qualityNotes: Contains anchovies and barley malt vinegar. Lea & Perrins is the benchmark; vegan versions exist.

yellow-pepper.name: Yellow peppers
yellow-pepper.qualityNotes: Firm, unblemished, not sprouting; loose is usually cheaper per kg than pre-packed.
